assets.theme: Mycelium-Bound Hemp Shive Board with Organic Fiber Boundaries
assets.palette: oatmeal ivory, natural hemp beige, soft umber, pale clay
assets.prompt: Create a reusable high-resolution biomaterial texture for a circular packaging art director designing a sustainability report cover and a biodegradable packaging concept board. Depict a single dry, pressed mycelium-bound hemp-shive panel as a continuous surface, with short irregular lignocellulosic chips embedded in a fine off-white fungal binder. Show natural pores, varied tiny fiber orientations, delicate compressed boundaries, occasional warm brown plant fragments, and convincing matte thickness cues without depicting active fuzzy mold or growing mushrooms. Compose as a horizontal 16:9 close-range surface study with the camera almost perpendicular to the material. Let the subtle cellular and fiber structure become clearer toward the right edge, keeping the left forty-five percent visually quiet for typography added later. Apply Scientific Material Macro Photography with natural oatmeal, hemp beige, pale clay and softly shaded micro-relief. Use broad diffuse studio daylight with only shallow consistent directional shadowing. The full frame should crop flexibly for websites and packaging layouts, without artificial repetitions or any claim of tileable edges. Keep the image original and unbranded, with no text, logos, labels, watermarks, objects or fabricated material diagrams.
assets.negative_prompt: living fungus, mushroom caps, glossy plastic, cotton paper fibers only, faux moss, repeated stamp tiles, writing

Thick ochre pigment appears at the beginning of the drag, breaking into believable fine parallel bristle trails, sparse skipped fibers, granular dry deposits and feathered edges as the brush runs out of paint. Art style: Fine Art Surface Reproduction Photography, tactile analog brush mechanics, refined natural imperfections, even warm light and true pigment surface relief.
